title: Bokurano: Ours
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Fifteen children exploring a seaside cave meet a stranger who invites them to 'play a game' piloting a giant robot against alien invaders, and they sign his contract. They learn that each battle is piloted by one child, who dies after it, and that losing means the destruction of their entire world. Mohiro Kitoh's seinen tragedy gives each child a chapter arc confronting death, family secrets, abuse and what their life has meant.
life_message: Facing a death you cannot escape, a life gains meaning through what you choose to protect and how you treat others in the time left.

content.note: Robot battles destroy cities and kill thousands; every pilot dies (AniList Death Game, Gore 70; MU Play or Die Situation, Violence).
Children facing certain death; cosmic horror premise (AniList Cosmic Horror 100, Tragedy 98; MU Despair, Mind Break).
Sexual abuse of a child character, including rape and resulting pregnancy (AniList Rape 60 spoiler; MU Sexual Abuse 22 votes, Rape, Teen Pregnancy). MU also lists gang rape (7 votes; to verify).
Despair, revenge and bullying among doomed children (AniList Bullying 56; MU Mind Break, Psychological Trauma, Child Abuse).
A child uses the robot for revenge (to verify).

dominant: Existential meaning before death; critique of sacrificing the few for the many

folkways.japan: Acceptance of fate (shikata ga nai) and self-sacrifice for the group reflect Japanese cultural themes explored rather than endorsed.

delivery.evidence: Meaning before death carried by each child's arc; no review on delivery found (to verify).
delivery.note: Its critique of sacrificing the few is carried by the children's stories rather than stated, per summaries.

winners_losers: No one survives the contract; abusers and exploitative adults lose sympathy, and the children who protect others in their last act get it.
